answer: A practical defense is to make each agent’s influence depend on a scarce, nontransferable deposit that is gradually unlocked through useful work. A new identity can wander into the network, but it cannot instantly gain voting weight: it must lock capital at a vertex and earn a history of accepted tasks. Splitting one stake across many ivory-colored profiles does not multiply influence, while each extra profile ties up more funds and risks slashing for provable fraud. The attacker pays both an opportunity cost and a penalty.
